blame.commit_message: Seed bug: add_item() returns list.append()'s result (always None) instead of the cart

hypothesis.root_cause: The add_item() function returns the result of list.append(), which always returns None in Python, instead of returning the updated cart object. Any caller that does `cart = add_item(cart, item)` (or similar reassignment) will overwrite their cart reference with None. A subsequent call to add_item() (or any code) that then calls `cart.items` on that None value raises 'AttributeError: NoneType object has no attribute items', matching the exact error and line reported.
evidence: Git blame commit 01d5edcc52 explicitly states: 'Seed bug: add_item() returns list.append()'s result (always None) instead of the cart' - a direct admission of the bug.
Code context shows `return cart.items.append(item)`; list.append() always returns None in Python, so add_item always returns None.

Stack trace error occurs at cart.py line 10 inside add_item, on `cart.items` access failing with 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'items', consistent with cart having been set to None from a prior add_item call whose return value was mistakenly used as the new cart.
No prior similar incidents in memory, so this assessment relies solely on the blame message and code inspection, not on precedent.
hypothesis.suggested_fix_direction: Modify add_item() to mutate cart.items via append() as a separate statement and then explicitly `return cart` (the cart object itself), rather than returning the append() call's result. Also audit callers to ensure they aren't reassigning cart from add_item's return value in a way that assumed a non-None cart was always returned.

fix.commit_message: fix: return cart object from add_item instead of list.append() result
fix.summary: add_item() previously returned the result of list.append(), which is always None, causing callers that reassign `cart = add_item(cart, item)` to lose their cart reference. Fixed to append as a separate statement and explicitly return cart.
